deep.reconstruction:
Setting. r_nu(A) is the sequence of moduli of the eigenvalues of a compact operator A. s_nu = r_nu(|A|) are its singular values. S_p(A) = sum s_nu^p, as on the previous page. L^p(𝔄) is the Schatten-type class (the machine reading 'L^1' is probably 'L^p'). Â is the eigenvalue sequence of A, viewed up to permutation. Sigma_p is the space of such sequences with the l^p-type topology.

Theorem. If A_i -> A in L^p, then Â_i -> Â in Sigma_p. In other words, the eigenvalue sequence depends continuously on the operator in Schatten p-norm.

Key lemma (uniform smallness of the small eigenvalues). For every eps > 0 there are rho > 0 and i_0 such that for i >= i_0, sum over r_nu(A_i) <= rho of r_nu(A_i)^p is at most eps. Together with convergence of the finitely many large eigenvalues (by continuity of isolated spectral data), this gives convergence in Sigma_p.

Proof of the lemma.
1. Take omega convex and increasing: omega(t) = e^{pt} for t <= log rho, and the tangent line beyond, i.e. omega(t) = rho^p (1 + p(t - log rho)) = rho^p log[e (e^t/rho)^p].
2. Weyl's majorant theorem for convex increasing functions of log|lambda| gives sum omega(log r_nu) <= sum omega(log s_nu).
3. Written out: sum_{r<=rho} r^p + rho^p sum_{r>=rho} log[e (r/rho)^p] is bounded by the same expression in the s_nu.
4. Margin note: |A_i| -> |A| in L^p, i.e. continuity of the absolute value on Schatten classes. This reduces everything to A_i >= 0.
5. For A_i >= 0 one must show the whole left-hand expression is uniformly <= eps. The struck-through plan splits this into two parts:
   a) for a fixed sequence, rho^p sum_{r>=rho} log[e(r/rho)^p] -> 0 as rho -> 0;
   b) uniformity in i (done on the next page via convergence of S_p(A_i) and of the large eigenvalues).
6. Proof of a), by Stieltjes integration by parts with the counting function n(r) = #{nu : r_nu >= r}: the quantity equals rho^p n(rho) + p rho^p ∫_rho^∞ n(r)/r dr. The first term tends to 0 because sum r_nu^p < ∞ (the standard Chebyshev/tail argument). The second term is treated on the next page.

Purpose. Part of Grothendieck's 1953 study of eigenvalue distributions of operators in Schatten / noncommutative L^p classes. This connects to his later Fredholm-theory work (eigenvalues of nuclear and p-summing operators).
errors: The page's own computations are correct. The integration by parts holds since log[e(r/rho)^p] = 1 + p log(r/rho), and rho^p n(rho) -> 0 is standard.

On the NEXT page, the second term is handled by claiming that ∫ n(r)/r^{1+p} dr < ∞ implies 'a fortiori' ∫_0^∞ n(r)/r dr < ∞. This is false: n(r) >= 1 near 0 for a nonzero sequence, so ∫_0 n(r)/r dr diverges. The conclusion is still true by dominated convergence, since 1_{r>rho} rho^p n(r)/r <= n(r) r^{p-1}, which is integrable with integral sum r_nu^p / p.

The reduction to A_i >= 0 uses continuity of A -> |A| in L^p. This is true, but on this page it is only asserted (marginal note) and not proved. The previous page shows Grothendieck was still conjecturing the relevant operator-Hölder inequality.
Part b) requires rho not to be an accumulation point of eigenvalue moduli of A, or a limiting argument. This is a minor gap, handled implicitly on the next page.

ideas.what: Weyl's majorant inequality sum phi(log|lambda_nu|) <= sum phi(log s_nu) for convex increasing phi, applied with a tailored piecewise exp/linear phi
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's majorant theorem (log-majorization of eigenvalues by singular values)
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) / Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), unsure

ideas.what: Continuity of the eigenvalue sequence (modulo permutation) as a function of the operator in Schatten p-norm
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of the spectrum / eigenvalue sequences in Schatten classes (l^p-continuity of eigenvalues)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gohberg–Krein school (1960s); Markus; standard in Simon's 'Trace Ideals'

ideas.what: Continuity of A -> |A| in L^p, used to reduce to positive operators
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of the absolute value on Schatten classes (Powers–Størmer, Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak type estimates)

ideas.what: Tail estimate via the counting function n(r) and Stieltjes integration by parts

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck had a proof, via Weyl's majorant theorem with a cleverly chosen convex function, that eigenvalue sequences depend continuously on the operator in Schatten p-classes. The result itself is now standard but usually credited to later operator theorists. The specific proof trick is not widely known, though it is close in spirit to standard arguments.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck was working in Weyl–Schatten eigenvalue theory and noncommutative L^p before the Gohberg–Krein systematization.

missed.claim: This page relies on |A_i| -> |A| in L^p. The previous page conjectures ‖|h^r - k^r|‖^{1/r} <= ‖h - k‖ for 0<r<1, which is an operator-Hölder (Powers–Størmer / Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak) inequality, in 1953.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority note: an early formulation of operator-Hölder continuity of power functions in Schatten norms, proved only in the 1970s.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and standard by modern lights: Weyl majorant plus tail estimates. It is a mildly notable early (1953) unpublished treatment of eigenvalue continuity in Schatten classes, connected to the operator-Hölder conjecture on the previous page. It is not new mathematics today.
transcription_corrections: 'L^1(𝔄)' in the theorem is likely 'L^p(𝔄)', since the target is Σ_p and p is used throughout.
'log e(...)^p' should be read as log[e·(·)^p], i.e. 1 + p log(·).
In the integration by parts, the bracket term is [-n(r) log e(r/ρ)^p] evaluated from ρ+0 to +∞.
The bottom line reads roughly 'et il est bien connu, puisque Σ r_ν^p < +∞, que ρ^p n(ρ) → 0'.
The left margin note concerns |A_i| → |A| (and A_i^+), justifying the reduction to positive operators.
